card.name: Bhangra
card.tagline: Energetic Punjabi harvest folk dance driven by the dhol
card.profile: Bhangra is a vigorous folk dance of the Punjab region of the Indian subcontinent, especially associated with the spring Vaisakhi harvest festival (Wikipedia). Dancers perform energetic kicks, leaps and shoulder movements to short sung couplets (boliyan) and the syncopated beat of the double-headed dhol drum (Britannica). Its purest traditional form is traced to the Sialkot area; modern staged bhangra developed in the 1950s, notably patronized by the Maharaja of Patiala who requested a performance in 1953 (Wikipedia). The Punjabi diaspora spread bhangra worldwide, fusing it with hip-hop, house and reggae.
card.insight: Originally a men's dance, bhangra drew its name from bhang (hemp), a Vaisakhi harvest product, and second-generation diaspora Punjabi women later embraced it, sometimes at the expense of the traditional women's giddha (Britannica).
